newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA in the market for Airbus A3XX.
newsitem.headline: BA in the market for Airbus A3XX.

text.p: British Airways Plc Chief Executive Bob Ayling said on Thursday he was "in the market" for the Airbus Industrie very large plane, the $8.0 billion A3XX project.
Ayling told a news briefing that he had spoken to Airbus Managing Director Jean Pierson "personally" and told him that BA was "in the market to acquire an aircraft of that size".

"I believe that Airbus will build that aircraft, and very much hope they will. I am sure that it is the aircraft of the future and we must see what the specification of the aircraft is, how much it costs," he said.
"If Airbus can produce an aircraft which is the right aircraft and it is successful in competition with other manufacturers, then we can buy Airbus," Ayling said.
Boeing Co has put its very large aircraft project on ice.
Ayling said that British Airways' regional operations in Birmingham and Manchester were "on the point" of ordering new aircraft because they had successfully restructured their business.
For these planes, Airbus is also among the possible manufacturers.
British Airways has for years been a very faithful Boeing client, operating only a few Airbus planes it acquired with British Caledonian.

A spokesman for Airbus in Toulouse said that British Airways was one of 12 companies on a working group of airlines involved in developing the A3XX, a 500-seat long-range aircraft scheduled for 2003. He declined to name the other companies in the group.
Ayling was in France for a regular meeting with the management of the recently merged TAT/Air Liberte French carrier, which is 70-percent owned by BA.
He said the merged group would be called Air Liberte, after the airline BA acquired with Banque Rivaud from the receivers and put under the management of TAT head Marc Rochet.
Ayling declined to comment on the industrial action at TAT/Air Liberte, with some flying staff on an indefinite strike over working conditions.
But he did say that an airline needed to have a competitive cost structure in order to be profitable and the structure at TAT was not competitive.
He added he wanted the French unit to reach break-even as soon as possible and declined to give a figure for the expected loss for 1997.
"That will be part of the BA first quarter results which are due in May," he said.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain. Aerospatiale and Deutsche Airbus have 38 percent each. British Aerospace Plc has 20 percent and CASA of Spain four percent.
